speak: Nineteen seventy-seven. The first general manager of a small computer company hands out employee numbers.
sub: 1977. The first general manager of a small computer company hands out employee numbers.

speak: Number one goes to the engineer who designed the computer. Number two, to his partner.
sub: Number one goes to the engineer who designed the computer. Number two, to his partner.

speak: The partner gets angry. He wants to be number one. As it was told later, he even cries.
sub: The partner gets angry. He wants to be number one. As it was told later, he even cries.

speak: The manager, Mike Scott, gives him zero: before number one. But the payroll bank wouldn't accept zero, so on paper he remained number two.
sub: The manager, Mike Scott, gives him zero: before number one. But the payroll bank wouldn't accept zero, so on paper he remained number two.

speak: The partner's name was Steve Jobs.
sub: The partner's name was Steve Jobs.

speak: Today that company is worth around five trillion dollars. This is the story of Apple, told through its strangest anecdotes.
sub: Today that company is worth around five trillion dollars. This is the story of Apple, told through its strangest anecdotes.

speak: Chapter one. A call to the Vatican.
sub: CHAPTER 1 — A CALL TO THE VATICAN

speak: It all begins with two Steves: Wozniak, an electronics genius, and Jobs, five years younger. In nineteen seventy-one they read something incredible in a magazine.
sub: It all begins with two Steves: Wozniak, an electronics genius, and Jobs, five years younger. In 1971 they read something incredible in a magazine.

speak: Let's go to the chalkboard. Back then, telephone exchanges talked to each other using sounds.
sub: Let's go to the chalkboard. Back then, telephone exchanges talked to each other using sounds.

speak: A tone of twenty-six hundred hertz meant: free line. And a toy whistle, a free prize inside a cereal box, made that exact tone.
sub: A 2600 Hz tone meant: free line. And a toy whistle, a free prize inside a cereal box, made that exact tone.

speak: If you blew it into the phone, the exchange handed you the line. And you could call anywhere in the world, for free.
sub: If you blew it into the phone, the exchange handed you the line. And you could call anywhere in the world, for free.

speak: The largest telephone network in the world was fooled by a cereal toy.
sub: The largest telephone network in the world was fooled by a cereal toy.

speak: Wozniak built a little blue box that made those tones. One day he called the Vatican and, with a fake accent, claimed to be Henry Kissinger. He asked to speak to the Pope.
sub: Wozniak built a little blue box that made those tones. One day he called the Vatican and, with a fake accent, claimed to be Henry Kissinger. He asked to speak to the Pope.

speak: According to Jobs, they actually sent someone to wake up the Pope. Then they burst out laughing, and were caught.
sub: According to Jobs, they actually sent someone to wake up the Pope. Then they burst out laughing, and were caught.

speak: Jobs sold about two hundred boxes. One built them and the other sold them. Apple already existed, even if it didn't have a name yet.
sub: Jobs sold about two hundred boxes. One built them and the other sold them. Apple already existed, even if it didn't have a name yet.

speak: Chapter two. Two Steves, one paycheck.
sub: CHAPTER 2 — TWO STEVES, ONE PAYCHECK

speak: In nineteen seventy-four, Jobs joined Atari, the hottest video game company around, as a technician.
sub: In 1974, Jobs joined Atari, the hottest video game company around, as a technician.

speak: He had a theory: since he ate almost only fruit, he didn't need to shower often. His coworkers did not agree.
sub: He had a theory: since he ate almost only fruit, he didn't need to shower often. His coworkers did not agree.

speak: Atari moved him to the night shift. Its founder, Nolan Bushnell, later said he got a bonus out of it: Wozniak came in at night to help him. Two Steves for the price of one.
sub: Atari moved him to the night shift. Its founder, Nolan Bushnell, later said he got a bonus out of it: Wozniak came in at night to help him. Two Steves for the price of one.

speak: Atari asked Jobs for a game using very few chips: Breakout. Wozniak designed it in four nights, barely sleeping.
sub: Atari asked Jobs for a game using very few chips: Breakout. Wozniak designed it in four nights, barely sleeping.

speak: Jobs told him they had been paid seven hundred dollars, and gave him half. According to Wozniak, the real bonus was around five thousand.
sub: Jobs told him they had been paid 700 dollars, and gave him half. According to Wozniak, the real bonus was around 5,000.

speak: He found out about ten years later, reading a book. He said he cried. And that if Jobs had just asked for the money, he would have given it to him.
sub: He found out about ten years later, reading a book. He said he cried. And that if Jobs had just asked for the money, he would have given it to him.

speak: Chapter three. April Fools' Day.
sub: CHAPTER 3 — APRIL FOOLS' DAY

speak: Apple was founded on April first, nineteen seventy-six. In the United States, April Fools' Day.
sub: Apple was founded on April 1, 1976. In the United States, April Fools' Day.

speak: There were three partners. The third, Ronald Wayne, forty-one years old, held ten percent. He drew the first logo: Isaac Newton reading under an apple tree.
sub: There were three partners. The third, Ronald Wayne, 41, held 10%. He drew the first logo: Isaac Newton reading under an apple tree.

speak: Twelve days later, frightened by potential debts, he sold his share for eight hundred dollars. He always said he didn't regret it.
sub: Twelve days later, frightened by potential debts, he sold his share for 800 dollars. He always said he didn't regret it.

speak: A local store had ordered fifty computers. To buy the parts, Jobs sold his van and Wozniak sold his scientific calculator.
sub: A local store had ordered 50 computers. To buy the parts, Jobs sold his van and Wozniak sold his calculator.

speak: The retail price: six hundred sixty-six dollars and sixty-six cents. More than a few saw the number of the beast.
sub: The retail price: 666.66 dollars. More than a few saw the number of the beast.

speak: There was nothing satanic about it. Wozniak simply liked repeating digits.
sub: There was nothing satanic about it. Wozniak simply liked repeating digits.

speak: Chapter four. The computer that didn't exist.
sub: CHAPTER 4 — THE COMPUTER THAT DIDN'T EXIST

speak: In nineteen seventy-seven, at a major computer fair in San Francisco, Apple unveiled the Apple Two.
sub: In 1977, at a major computer fair in San Francisco, Apple unveiled the Apple II.

speak: And Wozniak, in secret, handed out thousands of brochures for a spectacular machine: the Zaltair. It didn't exist. It was a parody of the Altair, the most famous computer of the day.
sub: And Wozniak, in secret, handed out thousands of brochures for a spectacular machine: the Zaltair. It didn't exist. It was a parody of the Altair.

speak: Jobs fell for it. He checked the comparison chart and felt proud: the Apple Two held its own. Wozniak told him the truth years later.
sub: Jobs fell for it. He checked the comparison chart and felt proud: the Apple II held its own. Wozniak told him the truth years later.

speak: Other surprises weren't on purpose. In nineteen eighty came the Apple Three, with no cooling fan, just as Jobs wanted. From the heat, chips popped right out of their sockets.
sub: Other surprises weren't on purpose. In 1980 came the Apple III, with no fan, as Jobs wanted. From the heat, chips popped out of their sockets.

speak: According to accounts from that era, some customers were advised to lift it a few inches and drop it. That pushed the chips back into place.
sub: According to accounts from that era, some customers were advised to lift it a few inches and drop it. That pushed the chips back into place.

speak: Tech support fit into a single word: drop it.
sub: Tech support fit into a single word: drop it.

speak: Chapter five. Better to be a pirate.
sub: CHAPTER 5 — BETTER TO BE A PIRATE

speak: To keep Apple from turning bureaucratic, Jobs repeated a line: it's better to be a pirate than to join the navy.
sub: To keep Apple from turning bureaucratic, Jobs repeated a line: it's better to be a pirate than to join the navy.

speak: The Macintosh team sewed a pirate flag and raised it on the roof. The rival team, building the Lisa computer, stole it and demanded a ransom.
sub: The Macintosh team sewed a pirate flag and raised it on the roof. The rival team, building the Lisa computer, stole it and demanded a ransom.

speak: At its unveiling in nineteen eighty-four, the Macintosh spoke on its own. And it mocked giant computers: never trust a computer you can't lift.
sub: At its unveiling in 1984, the Macintosh spoke on its own. And it mocked giant computers: never trust a computer you can't lift.

speak: Who drew what appeared on that screen? Susan Kare. Let's go to the chalkboard, because this hits close to home for this channel.
sub: Who drew what appeared on that screen? Susan Kare. Let's go to the chalkboard, because this hits close to home for this channel.

speak: The screen was a grid of tiny dots, black or white. One icon took up thirty-two by thirty-two: one thousand twenty-four little squares.
sub: The screen was a grid of tiny dots, black or white. One icon took up 32 by 32: 1,024 little squares.

speak: Kare didn't even have a computer to design on. She bought a two-dollar-and-fifty-cent graph paper notebook and colored every icon, square by square.
sub: Kare didn't have a computer to design on. She bought a $2.50 graph paper notebook and colored every icon, square by square.

speak: The most famous icons of their era were pixel art. And they were drawn with a pencil.
sub: The most famous icons of their era were pixel art. And they were drawn with a pencil.

speak: Chapter six. So sue me.
sub: CHAPTER 6 — SO SUE ME

speak: In nineteen eighty-five, after a clash with the board, Jobs left his own company. He founded another, NeXT, and paid one hundred thousand dollars for the logo.
sub: In 1985, after a clash with the board, Jobs left his own company. He founded another, NeXT, and paid $100,000 for the logo.

speak: Apple had another problem: the Beatles' company was also called Apple. To avoid lawsuits, it promised never to enter the music business.
sub: Apple had another problem: the Beatles' company was also called Apple. To avoid lawsuits, it promised never to enter the music business.

speak: But computers were making more and more sounds. In nineteen eighty-nine came another lawsuit, and lawyers vetted even the names of system alert sounds.
sub: But computers were making more and more sounds. In 1989 came another lawsuit, and lawyers vetted even the names of system sounds.

speak: Engineer Jim Reekes was told one of his sound names wouldn't pass legal review. He replied: so sue me. And he spelled the sound Sosumi.
sub: Engineer Jim Reekes was told one of his sound names wouldn't pass legal review. He replied: 'so sue me.' And he spelled the sound Sosumi.

speak: The lawyers approved it without realizing. More than thirty years later, that joke is still chiming on Macs.
sub: The lawyers approved it without realizing. More than thirty years later, that joke is still chiming on Macs.

speak: Chapter seven. One dollar a year.
sub: CHAPTER 7 — ONE DOLLAR A YEAR

speak: Without Jobs, Apple did worse and worse. By the mid-nineties it stood on the brink of bankruptcy.
sub: Without Jobs, Apple did worse and worse. By the mid-nineties it stood on the brink of bankruptcy.

speak: It bought NeXT to get an operating system, and with the company came Jobs. He asked for a salary of one dollar a year.
sub: It bought NeXT to get an operating system, and with the company came Jobs. He asked for a salary of one dollar a year.

speak: In nineteen ninety-seven he announced that Microsoft, the arch-rival, was investing one hundred fifty million dollars in Apple. Bill Gates appeared on a giant screen, and the audience booed.
sub: In 1997 he announced that Microsoft, the arch-rival, was investing $150 million in Apple. Bill Gates appeared on a giant screen, and the audience booed.

speak: Jobs also had his quirks. His silver sports car never had a license plate.
sub: Jobs also had his quirks. His silver sports car never had a license plate.

speak: According to a former Apple security chief, the law gave a grace period to put plates on a brand-new car. Jobs leased an identical one every six months.
sub: According to a former Apple security chief, the law gave a grace period to put plates on a new car. Jobs leased an identical one every six months.

speak: California traffic authorities later said it didn't quite work that way. What's certain is that he had saved Apple. And that the license plate never showed up.
sub: California traffic authorities said it didn't quite work that way. What's certain is that he had saved Apple. And that the plate never showed up.

speak: Chapter eight. Four thousand lattes.
sub: CHAPTER 8 — FOUR THOUSAND LATTES

speak: January two thousand seven. Jobs unveils the iPhone. The audience had no idea the prototype barely worked.
sub: January 2007. Jobs unveils the iPhone. The audience had no idea the prototype barely worked.

speak: It crashed and dropped signal, so the signal bars were hardcoded to always show five. And in the fifth row, engineers passed around a flask of whisky.
sub: It crashed and dropped signal, so the signal bars were hardcoded to always show five. And in the fifth row, engineers passed around a flask of whisky.

speak: Let's go to the chalkboard. Picture the phone's memory as a glass.
sub: Let's go to the chalkboard. Picture the phone's memory as a glass.

speak: Every open app pours water into it. Unfinished apps didn't give the water back, and when the glass overflowed, the phone froze.
sub: Every open app pours water into it. Unfinished apps didn't give the water back, and when the glass overflowed, the phone froze.

speak: If you sent an email and then browsed the web, it worked. The other way around, it crashed. So they mapped out one exact sequence: the golden path.
sub: If you sent an email and then browsed, it worked. The other way around, it crashed. So they mapped out one exact sequence: the golden path.

speak: The iPhone worked, as long as nobody stepped off the script.
sub: The iPhone worked, as long as nobody stepped off the script.

speak: To demo maps, Jobs called a real Starbucks live on stage. He ordered four thousand lattes to go, and hung up: wrong number.
sub: To demo maps, Jobs called a real Starbucks live on stage. He ordered 4,000 lattes to go, and hung up: wrong number.

speak: The first public phone call ever made on an iPhone was a prank call. Just like in the Vatican days.
sub: The first public phone call ever made on an iPhone was a prank call. Just like in the Vatican days.

speak: Chapter nine. Pirate or navy?
sub: CHAPTER 9 — PIRATE OR NAVY?

speak: Jobs passed away in two thousand eleven, at fifty-six. Tim Cook led Apple for the next fifteen years.
sub: Jobs passed away in 2011, at 56. Tim Cook led Apple for the next fifteen years.

speak: For Apple's fiftieth anniversary in two thousand twenty-six, Paul McCartney played at its headquarters. A Beatle, after nearly thirty years of lawsuits over the name.
sub: For Apple's 50th anniversary in 2026, Paul McCartney played at its headquarters. A Beatle, after nearly thirty years of lawsuits over the name.

speak: That year a new chief took over, engineer John Ternus. And Apple launched its first foldable iPhone.
sub: That year a new chief took over, engineer John Ternus. And Apple launched its first foldable iPhone.

speak: Today it's worth around five trillion dollars, battling NVIDIA for the title of most valuable company on Earth.
sub: Today it's worth around five trillion dollars, battling NVIDIA for the title of most valuable company on Earth.

speak: Jobs preferred pirates. But Apple is now one of the largest navies on the planet.
sub: Jobs preferred pirates. But Apple is now one of the largest navies on the planet.

speak: The question is whether it still has any pirate left in it.
sub: The question is whether it still has any pirate left in it.

speak: What do you think? What story would you like to see in the next episode? Let us know down in the comments.
sub: What do you think? What story would you like to see in the next episode? Let us know down in the comments.
